limitations: Esports matches from historical seasons, not modern ranked data.
No per-player kill event timestamps or true event-level WPA.
Round economy values may reflect a state after the round; timing must be verified before using as predictive features.
TeamSide is team number 1 or 2 in source game record, not attack/defense side.
Team1_Side blank during overtime because side choices cannot be inferred safely.
Round win types and post-round scores are outcomes and must never be predictive inputs for the same round.
Only games with verifiable abbreviation mappings and exactly 5 players per team retained.
Splits are chronological by series MatchID to avoid maps from the same series in different partitions.
Player models observe the finished scoreboard; predictions are retrospective associations
Heuristic index weights are equal, not learned causal contributions
Clutch and objective counts lack opportunity denominators
Confidence intervals resample series; limited to this historical test period
Train/validation historical rows have in-sample/fitting-period predictions; test rows are held out
Map slices measure temporal performance within maps, not unseen-map transfer
protocol: Train on supplied train. First half of validation series selects minimum log loss. Second half fits one temperature. Freeze; evaluate all predeclared candidates and selected calibrated model once on test. No test tuning.
